plan_a_advantages: Includes tempo runs to improve lactate threshold and running economy.
Incorporates hill sessions to build strength and power, essential for trail running.
Higher overall volume allows for greater physiological adaptation and potential for speed gains.
More varied workouts (long, tempo, hills, easy) provide a more well-rounded training stimulus.
plan_b_advantages: Lower volume may be suitable for athletes with a history of injury or those new to trail running.
Emphasis on easy running and cross-training can build a solid aerobic base without excessive stress.
Two rest days provide ample recovery time.
reasoning: Given the goal of becoming a *faster* trail runner, Plan A is the better choice. While Plan B focuses heavily on aerobic base building with a lot of easy running and cross-training, it lacks the intensity needed to improve speed. Plan A incorporates tempo runs and hill sessions, which are crucial for developing the speed and strength required for faster trail running. The higher volume in Plan A, while requiring more recovery, also provides more opportunity for adaptation and improvement in speed and endurance.
